name: weighted_provider_selection_v1
description: Replaced always-Groq-first with weighted random selection (30:15). Share numbers are the expected ratio, not measured.

name: half_open_before_fix
description: Original breaker: half_open fell through to return True, so every request after cooldown became a probe

name: half_open_after_fix
description: Fixed breaker: half_open returns False, so only the first request after cooldown is the probe

name: gemini_thought_signature_fix
description: Unified OpenAI-shaped schema was silently dropping Gemini's thought_signature on multi-turn tool calls, causing 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT on turn 2. Fixed by capturing it in normalize_tool_calls (from response.candidates[0].content.parts) and replaying it in convert_messages.

name: stuck_probe_fix
description: InvalidRequestError during a half_open probe never called record_success or record_failure, leaving the breaker permanently stuck in half_open. Added record_inconclusive to reset it back to open with a fresh cooldown instead, so a later request gets a genuine test.

name: rpm_tpm_leak_fix
description: select_provider used 'rpm.try_consume() and tpm.try_consume()' which spent an RPM slot even when the TPM check failed right after, silently leaking provider capacity. Split TokenBucket into can_consume (check) and consume (commit), checking both buckets before spending either. Verified with Groq forced to go first and a deliberately-too-small TPM budget.

name: bucket_breaker_cleanup
description: Removed conversation_provider_map, a leftover stickiness mechanism that did a worse, accidental version of what the circuit breaker already does properly (only remembered a failure after it happened, per-conversation, with no recovery awareness). Also caught and avoided a double allow_request() bug before shipping: having both select_provider and _try check the breaker would have blocked the exact provider select_provider had just approved, since the first call on an open+expired-cooldown breaker flips it to half_open, and the second call then sees half_open and rejects it.

name: cache_scope_privacy_fix
description: SemanticCache was a single global instance with no awareness of conversation_id or user. reviewer.py's internal review call (is_tool_related=False, no tools) was cache-eligible, and the cached text included real retrieved document passages plus a draft answer — a semantically similar reviewer call from a different user/document could receive someone else's document content back. Fixed by splitting into per-conversation caches (OrderedDict with LRU eviction, cap 500) and one explicit global cache, gated by a new cache_scope field the caller must opt into (conversation/global/none). Defaults to no caching, so the system fails safe until callers opt in.

name: conversation_stickiness_restored
description: Removing conversation_provider_map (earlier cleanup) assumed message-history replay made provider stickiness unnecessary, which holds for plain text but not for Gemini's thought_signature on tool calls. QueryMind's agent loop reuses one conversation_id across ~6 steps; without stickiness, a step could land on Groq (no signature) then a later step in the same loop could land on Gemini, which rejects replaying a function-call part with no signature. Restored stickiness via get_provider_for_conversation, built on the fixed can_consume/consume bucket pair, with re-pinning on fallback. Breaker is still checked exactly once, in _try, avoiding the earlier double-check bug.

name: postgres_persistence_verified
description: Cost/request tracking previously lived in an in-memory Python list, wiped on every Render restart/redeploy (and free-tier services spin down on idle, making this frequent, not rare). Moved to Postgres (Neon, free persistent tier) via asyncpg. Verified request_logs data survives a service restart.

name: proper_http_status_codes
description: Every failure mode (InvalidRequestError, TooLongError, all-providers-rate-limited, genuine server errors) returned a blanket 500, giving callers no way to distinguish 'retry this' from 'never retry this' from 'wait and retry.' Added AllProvidersRateLimitedError and mapped each exception type to its correct HTTP status: 400 for malformed requests, 413 for prompts too long for any provider, 429 for temporary capacity exhaustion, 500 reserved for genuinely unexpected failures. Also scoped log levels so expected rejections (400/413) log at info, not error, keeping the error log reserved for real bugs.

name: gateway_phase1_2_before
description: Baseline before the per-deployment redesign: live /metrics/summary on Render, 2026-10-01 to 2026-11-17, 1,390 requests. Gemini's breaker flapped (98 opens, 6 closes), 190 requests failed with AllProvidersRateLimitedError, and p95 latency came from queue waits plus 2 s in-place retry sleeps instead of failing over.

name: gateway_phase1_2_after
description: After Phases 1 and 2: deployments = key x model from deployments.yaml, Gemini dropped, Groq x3 + OpenRouter x2 pooled, in-place retries removed (fail over at once), per-deployment daily counter, and every attempt logged to attempt_logs. Measured with QueryMind's 50-question eval, 165 gateway requests. Caveat: 1 user, sequential, versus all traffic in the baseline; the 10-user target is still untested.

name: invalid_tool_call_classification
description: Groq's HTTP 400 tool_use_failed was mapped to ProviderUnavailableError, so a bad output from the model counted as the model being down: 3 in a row opened the groq:gpt-oss-20b breaker and blocked all 3 healthy keys. Most of these requests succeeded on the next sample, so InvalidToolCallError became its own class: the breaker marks the provider reachable, no key cooldown, the router tries another key, and only 3 in a row returns 502 invalid_tool_call.

name: gateway_capacity_1_instance
description: Mock capacity test: one gateway process, memory store, DB off, against a mock provider with unlimited quota and 400 +/- 150 ms latency, so only the gateway can be the bottleneck. Linear up to 50 users at about 2,500 calls/min with p95 under 1 s; the knee is between 50 and 100 users, where queueing and load shedding start. That is 30-60x QueryMind's target load, so real limits are provider quota, not the gateway.

name: redis_state_store_before
description: Same mock capacity test at 50 users with all mutable state (meters, cooldowns, breakers, health, sticky pins) in the in-process MemoryStore. Fast, but a second instance would double-spend quota and a restart loses everything.

name: redis_state_store_after
description: Same test with RedisStore (local Redis): meters updated atomically by Lua scripts, breaker/cooldown/health by optimistic CAS. State survives restarts and is shared across instances, at a cost of about 22% throughput and 1 s of p95 per instance. The cause is about 37 mostly sequential Redis commands per gateway call (P22), not Redis itself.

name: scale_out_2_instances
description: Two gateway processes sharing one Redis, 25 users each. Same latency as one memory instance at 50 users, and the mock provider saw zero 429s across all 6,015 calls, so the shared meters stop the instances from double-spending quota.
